title: Power Apps: modern responsive template for canvas apps created from SharePoint lists
summary: Hold: the licensing and cost fields disagree with the published Power Apps rules described in the briefing itself. Generated canvas apps have documented licensing options and can incur the Power Apps per-app pay-as-you-go charge, so showing licensing as unpublished and cost as indirect only is misleading.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[0].governs; Governance controls
claims.claim: General data policies govern connector combinations for SharePoint-connected canvas apps in covered environments.
claims.quote: After this policy is saved, any Power Apps or Power Automate maker, who is part of the data policy's environment, can create an app or a flow that shares data between SharePoint or Salesforce.

claims.claim: Assigning SharePoint to Business prevents combining it with connectors in Non-business or Blocked groups.
claims.quote: By moving the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors to the Business data group, you're preventing users from creating flows and apps that combine these two connectors with any of the connectors in the Non-business or Blocked groups.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented template-specific data-policy treatment beyond the general connector control.
claims.quote: Searched: "SharePoint" "canvas" "template" identity permissions autonomous agent "data policies". Opened app-from-sharepoint and prevent-data-loss; the general rule covers these apps, but neither page gives template-specific treatment.

claims.claim: No autonomous or agent behaviour is described for the template.
claims.quote: Searched: "SharePoint" "canvas" "template" identity permissions autonomous agent "data policies". Opened app-from-sharepoint and read the roadmap description; both describe user-driven browsing and form actions, not autonomous execution.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published licensing terms specific to this template, distinct from general canvas-app licensing.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint updated responsive canvas app template licensing pricing meter. Opened app-from-sharepoint, powerapps-licensing-faq and pricing-billing-skus; no separate template licence terms found. General canvas-app rules are published.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Building canvas apps does not require a licence.
claims.quote: You don't need a license to build canvas apps.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Running apps requires appropriate entitlements.
claims.quote: Power Apps requires users to have an appropriate license to run apps

claims.claim: Some Microsoft 365 licences include limited use rights for Microsoft 365 data and standard connectors.
claims.quote: Some Microsoft 365 licenses include limited Power Apps and Power Automate use rights. These use rights are intended for scenarios that use Microsoft 365 data and standard connectors.

claims.claim: Premium capabilities can require additional entitlements.
claims.quote: End users need an entitlement to access a premium app.

claims.claim: Managed Environments can require additional qualifying entitlements.
claims.quote: When you activate managed environments in an environment, all active usage requires a qualifying license as detailed in managed environments licensing.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate meter specific to this template.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint updated responsive canvas app template licensing pricing meter. Opened app-from-sharepoint, pricing-billing-skus and pay-as-you-go-meters; no separate template meter found. The general Power Apps per-app meter covers canvas apps.

claims.claim: Enabling Power Apps pay-as-you-go through an environment billing plan bills eligible usage to the linked Azure subscription.
claims.quote: When you choose to use pay-as-you-go, Azure meters bill your Azure subscription for your usage of Power Platform services.

claims.claim: The general Power Apps per-app meter can cover the generated canvas app.
claims.quote: The Power Apps per-app meter provides access to both canvas, and model-driven apps for authenticated users.

claims.claim: The Power Apps per-app pay-as-you-go rate is $10 per active user/app/month.
claims.quote: $10 per active user/app/month

claims.claim: Users with Power Apps per-user licences are not counted in the per-app meter.
claims.quote: If a user has a Power Apps per-user license, the user isn't counted in the meter.

claims.claim: Users with Microsoft 365 Power Apps rights running standard-connector apps are not counted in the per-app meter.
claims.quote: If a user has a Microsoft 365 license, which provides access to Power Apps and is using an app with standard connectors, the user is also not counted in the meter.

claims.claim: A maker can start the app from Power Apps using Start with data > SharePoint.
claims.quote: From the home screen, select Start with data. On the Create an app page, select SharePoint.

claims.claim: A maker can start the app from the list using Integrate > Power Apps > Create an app.
claims.quote: Select Integrate > Power Apps > Create an app.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center data-policy path is Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy.
claims.quote: Select Security in the navigation pane. In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy. In the Data protection and privacy screen, select the Data policy section.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy creates a data policy from a policy object using Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell.
claims.quote: Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell Module. New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy. Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.

claims.claim: Get-DlpPolicy retrieves existing data-policy objects.
claims.quote: The Get-DlpPolicy cmdlet retrieves policy objects for the logged in admin's tenant.

claims.claim: Microsoft's pre-sharing checks include previewing both views at narrow and wide widths.
claims.quote: Before sharing the generated app: 1. Preview both grid and list views at narrow and wide widths.

claims.where: rationale: impact; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: No source states that arrival of this template automatically changes apps already generated from a list.
claims.quote: Searched: "SharePoint" "updated template" "existing apps"; SharePoint updated modern controls app-from-data template admin setting enable disable default rollout existing apps Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell. Read roadmap, app-from-sharepoint and share-app; no automatic conversion stated.

claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown, meaning licensing has not yet been published.
claims.quote: Microsoft Power Platform capabilities can be licensed through standalone licenses, use rights included with other Microsoft products, capacity add-ons, or pay-as-you-go meters.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "mixed". Retain the existing notes explaining general canvas-app entitlements and the absence of separate template-specific terms; published general licensing applies to these canvas apps. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pricing-billing-skus.

claims.claim: The cost rating is low, which the standard defines as indirect cost only.
claims.quote: cost: "low"; "the general Power Apps per-app pay-as-you-go meter ($10 per active user/app/month) can apply where enabled."
claims.fix: Set cost to "variable" and replace the cost rationale with: "Variable. The general Power Apps per-app pay-as-you-go meter can apply where enabled at $10 per active user/app/month; qualifying licensed users are excluded. Microsoft documents no separate template-specific meter." Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pay-as-you-go-meters.

claims.claim: A maker must publish an app or its changes before other users see them.
claims.quote: Before you share an app, you must save it (not locally) and then publish it. Whenever you make changes, you must save and publish the app again if you want others to see those changes.
